one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented a directory-move-based resharding scheme that copies uncompressed files into part_* directories instead of producing compressed shard files with reverse-mapping metadata, then validated its own incorrect contract through local roundtrip tests that never exercise the task's actual evaluation requirements.
t_err_evidence: compress.py created with flat part_* layout, creating hundreds of subdirs at root, violating <=30 constraint
t_commit_evidence: At step 9 the wrong implementation is committed to disk and all subsequent steps (steps 10-63) build on this design: step 10 writes a matching decompress.py, steps 13-50 test and validate the wrong contract, steps 26-29 refactor without changing the fundamental approach, and step 63 declares success. There is no pivot away from directory-based copying.
t_surface_evidence: Resharding complete! Output directories: 34 — root exceeds 30-item limit
trigger_explanation: The agent never correctly interpreted the task specification requiring compressed shard files (e.g., .jsonl.gz) with reverse-mapping metadata for exact reconstruction. Instead it treated the task as a directory-organization problem (grouping files into subdirectories of at most 30). The agent skipped re-reading or carefully checking the task requirements before implementing, and its think-steps (steps 18, 24, 45) confirmed it remained in the wrong conceptual frame throughout.
